content.text:
`System.out.println` now exists only inside `ConsoleLogger`, which is the correct single point of responsibility. Here's what was built and why each decision was made:

---

**`SimulationLogger`** — three-level interface (`info`, `warn`, `error`) rather than a single `log(level, message)` method. Separate methods are more ergonomic for call sites and avoid importing or referencing an enum at every use.

**`ConsoleLogger`** — the default. Prefixes each line with `[INFO]`, `[WARN]`, or `[ERROR]` so level is visible without any logging framework. This is where the two former `System.out.println` calls now live.

**`SilentLogger`** — swallows all messages. Useful when running the simulation in a test or batch context where console noise is unwanted.

**`CompositeLogger`** — satisfies the "register logs to different outputs" requirement. A caller builds a composite, adds as many `SimulationLogger` implementations as needed (console, file, a Swing `JTextArea`, etc.), and passes it once to the builder. The composite fans every message out to all registered delegates.

**`SimulatorConfig`** — gains a `private final SimulationLogger logger` field. Storing the logger on the config keeps it immutable and co-located with all other build-time decisions. `getLogger()` exposes it.

**`Simulator.Builder`** — gains a `SimulationLogger logger` field defaulting to `new ConsoleLogger()` so existing code with no `.logger(...)` call behaves identically to before. The `logger(SimulationLogger)` setter enables the fluent override. `buildConfig()` now calls `logger.warn(...)` for the two validation messages.

**`Simulator.getLogger()`** — a convenience accessor that delegates to `config.getLogger()`. Because both `PopulationManager` and `Weather` already hold a `Simulator` reference, they can call `simulator.getLogger().info(...)` for any future log statements without any new wiring.
